text: Log in at another Aimparency server from the page that shows its space: a login granted to that page, kept in the browser
description:
Felix 2026-11-15: writes across servers should be supported; the UI can deliver an account for that server, which means using the same key on various Aimparency servers.

Plan (Claude, from the discussion):
- The browser key (automatic accounts, 383e8949) is the identity across servers. When you act on a space of another server (a linked space opened in place, an offer to it), the page signs in there with the same key (keyChallenge/keyLogin): same public key = same person on every server; names stay per server.
- Writes from other sites, bound to where the token was issued: today a server refuses every write from another origin, even with a valid token (32ba03c0). Instead a server remembers the origin a token was issued to and accepts that token's writes only from that origin; any other origin stays read-only.
- Rights stay with each server: signing in elsewhere gives an account, not rights. There you are a guest until the space's owner grants write access; notes and offers (b7e0b972) work as for any guest.
- The UI shows on which servers you are signed in.

Trust: a browser key lives in one site's storage, so whoever runs that server could serve code that signs as you elsewhere. Acceptable for an automatic guest identity. For an identity independent of any server, the wallet login (abadab76) already exists: the key sits in the wallet, each signature is approved.

Also answers "reading needs an account" (a possible server setting, discussed 2026-11-15, would be an exception to "no private graphs" on 8faf6a70): such a server can still be opened in place from another server, because the page signs in there with the same key.

Felix 2026-11-16: rather (or also) "log in to that server via token": the main space server's page gets a login for the other server, e.g. a new tab with a challenge that redirects back. Super easy for the user: an expanded space of another server is read without login; when something is about to change, ask for the login there in one click. The UI aggregates logins for several servers; its own server never sees them. Logging out logs out of all servers.

Built (Claude 2026-11-16), instead of the shared browser key above (a key is per origin and cannot be carried over):
- b.org: auth.grantSite gives a token bound to the asking site's origin (Token.site). It works only from that origin's pages (Origin header), writes what the account writes and leaves notes, nothing of the account's own business (no logins, tokens, spaces, owner settings). Granting again replaces it; listed and revocable with the agent logins.
- a.org's page: a drag/edit on a read-only space of b.org opens "Log in at b.org" (ConnectServerModal); one click opens b.org/?connect-site=…&connect-state=… (ConnectSiteModal: log in there if needed, Allow); the token comes back by postMessage to exactly a.org and is kept in localStorage (utils/server-logins.ts).
- Every expanded space loads into the store (local or remote tRPC client, utils/remote-trpc.ts), marked writable or not; requests about its ideas are routed to its server (utils/idea-spaces.ts), writes to a read-only one ask for the login. Clicking its ideas stays in the UI.
- Logging out (or discarding the account) also logs out of every other server.

Open: private reading (all spaces are public to read for now); a visitor without an account here has no menu to see/log out of other servers' logins; a signed account-linking statement / wallet as server-independent identity later.
